facts.text: On this date in 1945, Sukarno declared Indonesian independence — but the Dutch refused to recognize it and fought a four-year war to reclaim the colony before finally conceding in 1949.
On August 17, 1960, Gabon became independent from France. It was the 14th African nation to gain independence that single year, a pace of decolonization with no parallel in recorded history.
Tokyo's greater metropolitan area holds 37 million people — more than the entire population of Canada — yet its murder rate is lower than that of Luxembourg.
More people live within 200 kilometers of Shanghai than in the entire United States.
Mongolia is the world's most sparsely populated sovereign nation, with roughly 2 people per square kilometer, yet its capital Ulaanbaatar holds nearly half the country's entire population.
On August 17, 1998, Russia defaulted on its domestic debt and devalued the ruble — triggering the collapse of Long-Term Capital Management, a hedge fund run by two Nobel laureates.
On August 17, 1971, Nixon formally ended dollar-gold convertibility, closing the 'gold window' and ending Bretton Woods — a decision made over a single weekend at Camp David.

The New York Stock Exchange was founded in 1792 under a buttonwood tree on Wall Street. The 24 brokers who signed the agreement set a fixed commission rate — essentially the first known price-fixing cartel in American finance.
Saudi Aramco briefly surpassed $2 trillion in market value in 2022, making it worth more than the entire GDP of Italy. It is the most profitable company in recorded corporate history.

During the 2008 financial crisis, the Reserve Primary Fund — a money market fund considered as safe as cash — 'broke the buck,' falling below $1 per share. The panic it triggered nearly froze the entire global credit system within 48 hours.
On this date in 1977, the Soviet icebreaker Arktika became the first surface ship to reach the North Pole — powered by nuclear reactors, it melted through ice three meters thick.
On August 17, 1966, NASA's Lunar Orbiter 1 took the first photograph of Earth from the Moon's vicinity, showing our planet as a crescent hung over the lunar surface.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces the lining of your small intestine every two to four days. The cells that digest your lunch today did not exist last week.
Light takes eight minutes to travel from the Sun to Earth, but up to 100,000 years to travel from the Sun's core to its surface, trapped by the density of plasma.
On this date in 1969, Woodstock ended — meaning everyone who attended is now older than the festival was when it happened, yet the mud still feels recent.
Augustus Caesar died on August 17, 14 AD. The Roman Empire he left behind outlasted the time between his death and today by over 500 years.
The University of Oxford was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Lectures began around 1096; Tenochtitlan wasn't founded until 1325.
On August 17, 1945, Sukarno declared Indonesian independence — after 350 years of Dutch rule, the document was typed on a borrowed typewriter.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; the pyramid rose around 2560 BC.

Sonder (n.): the sudden realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast linguists now debate whether invented words can become real ones this quickly.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. Untranslatable, it carries grief, nostalgia, and yearning simultaneously — a single word doing the work of a sentence.
On this day in 1945, George Orwell submitted 'Animal Farm' to his publisher — a man who had just coined the word 'doublethink' and would soon give English 'Newspeak,' 'thoughtcrime,' and 'unperson.'
Petrichor (n.): the smell of rain on dry earth. Coined in 1964 by Australian scientists Bear and Thomas, from Greek petra (stone) and ichor (the fluid in the veins of the gods).

On this day in 1896, gold was discovered in the Klondike, flooding English with 'sourdough' — an old-timer who wintered in the north — a word that slept in obscurity for a century before bread revived it.

On August 17, 2017, Bitcoin Cash forked from Bitcoin at block 478,558. The first BCH block was mined by ViaBTC and contained the message 'Welcome to the world, BCH' embedded in its coinbase transaction.
On August 17, 2020, Ethereum's Uniswap v2 crossed $1B in total liquidity for the first time — a threshold it hit without a single company, order book, or market maker in the traditional sense.

Bitcoin's timelock opcode OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY sat unused in the codebase for over a year before activation in BIP 65 (2015). Satoshi originally included a version of it, then quietly disabled it in an early commit.
The Ethereum genesis block on July 30, 2015 included 8,893 transactions — all pre-mines to crowdsale participants — processed before a single proof-of-work block was ever mined.

Miner Extractable Value (MEV) on Ethereum exceeded $1.38B extracted in a single year by 2022. The mechanism exploits transaction ordering visibility that Satoshi's whitepaper never modeled as an attack surface.

On this date in 2012, Alex Krizhevsky submitted AlexNet to the ImageNet competition. Its 15.3% top-5 error rate beat the runner-up by 10.8 percentage points — a margin so large the organizers assumed a reporting error.

Today in 2017, Google Brain published the Transformer paper. The architecture was designed for translation; its authors didn't anticipate it would become the substrate for nearly every major AI system within five years.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average U.S. homes, for a single model training pass.

Reinforcement learning from human feedback scales poorly with label noise: studies show that when annotator agreement drops below 70%, RLHF models reliably optimize for annotator confusion rather than the intended behavior.
The first neural network to beat a professional Go player, AlphaGo, was itself defeated by its successor AlphaGo Zero — trained with zero human game data — after just 40 days of self-play.
